placement.position_note: Interpretive placement on a GENERATED lot, not a recovered parcel. The lot geometry is the K7 plat module's — this project has never read Thompson's numbering off a sheet, and the side lot lines and the alley are conjectural even where the block face is not. The building stands 1.6 m back from its street edge, which is a typology for the period and not a measurement of this lot. The whole footprint — not its centre — is tested against the platted street corridors, against its own lot lines and against every other footprint in the dataset, so no invented building of this parcel stands in the roadway; clearing the roadway is not the same as standing on a recovered lot.

siding_exposure_m.note: INVENTED WITHIN A STOCK SET, NOT DERIVED. No source states the exposed face of any Chicago building's siding. The value is one of four period mill sidings — 4.5, 5, 5.5 or 6 in to the weather; this roof wears 5 in — dealt in this building's own parcel recipe: drawn on this record's stable key from the stocks its household class may hang (5 in or 5.5 in; T-1839, docs/LIBERTIES.md L352), then advanced within them so that no roof of the parcel standing within 60 m hangs the same course. It is NOT keyed to a construction season the way the named buildings' stocks are: this record's 1835-01-01 is the programme's count-unit convention and not a date anything was built, so keying to it would deal every anonymous roof in the town one stock. The separation is the surface variety T-0049 reconstructs, not a claim about 1835. docs/LIBERTIES.md L148 owns the invention and the recipe half is recorded beside it, under `tools/siding_stock.py`.

residents.name: The lodgers of Reconstructed H3 boarding house #01
residents.why: THE BED IS THE CLAIM. The lodging model puts 12 people in this house on an ordinary night and 28 when it was full, apportioned from the town model's own bracket. These people are here because the beds are, and for no other reason.
residents.basis: BEDS, AND ONE FAMILY. 3 of the people here took a bed and are not kin to each other or to anybody else under this roof — `data/residents/` cannot carry a person outside a household, so one record holds them all. The exception is the keeper and the 2 child(ren) on their card, who are a family and say so: every one of them carries `kin_of` naming the keeper.

citations.citation: Chicago · July 1835: Building Inventory and Architectural Reconstruction Specification. Prepared for Kevin Haas, August 2026.
what_it_supplies: A 665-roof production target with independently reconcilable group, district, level, and construction totals.
Thirty-five architectural family definitions with dimensional and massing bands.
District character, spacing, variation, finish, and chronology constraints for a July 1835 reconstruction.
A required distinction between named documentary landmarks and anonymous inferred infill.
what_it_does_not_supply: A surviving July 1835 building census or parcel-by-parcel roof register.
Exact locations, dimensions, appearance, occupants, or construction dates for anonymous roofs.
Authority to replace stronger building-specific evidence already represented in the dataset.

research_note: RECONSTRUCTED / GENERATED, NOT AN ATTESTED NAMED BUILDING. The block, its scheduled roof count and its family mix follow the 665-roof programme; exact presence, lot, position, footprint, finish and instance-level form are interpretive. The H3 boarding house resolves through the frame_tavern archetype, the crosswalk's placeholder for it; the canonical boarding_house_frame generator is not implemented. The tavern's own cues are not raised on it: no gallery, no frontispiece, no sign, and a kitchen door rather than a carriage door in the rear service wing.

fabric_basis.words: whitewashed clapboard on a braced frame under a weather-darkened roof — a boarding house, from the 1832–33 town (rule F-B: a boarding-house or tavern keeper's by its type)

sizes.upper_windows: ceil(28 crowded beds / 3 to a chamber) = 10, held to the crosswalk's 6-10 = 10, then to the 8 sashes a front of 9.51 m carries at 1.15 m a bay: 8 across the upper storey of the front and of the rear
sizes.stovepipes: ceil(12 ordinary beds / 3 to a stove) = 4, held to 2-6: 4
sizes.chimneys: not sized by the beds: the two brick stacks are the family's kitchen and common-room hearths, and the stoves the beds add go out through the roof as stovepipes

lodging.note: The town model puts a boarding house at 9 people on an ordinary night and 21 when full, from the 1840 household tail (p90 and p99 of 964 Chicago households). This building takes the share of its class's total that its 264 m² of enclosed floor (132 m² × 2 storeys) is of the class's floor area.
lodging.replaceable_by: Any source that states this house's rooms, beds or lodgers on a dated day: an advertisement counting its rooms, a traveller's account of how many it slept, a licence return. A stated capacity retires the apportioned one outright.

occupancy.statement: 8 on this card against an ordinary night's 12 beds: 5 seated here from elsewhere in the layer, where no source gives them a roof, 2 drawn against the order book's lodging buckets for beds that were standing empty, a keeper drawn for a roof this programme raised.
occupancy.empty_note: This house has a division and empty beds, and the order book has nothing left to draw them out of: every adult `lodging/none` cell of the south division is filled to what the book orders there. A person minted past that would be a person the town never ordered, so the beds stand empty and the order rather than the roof is what is short (T-1535).
occupancy.keeper_owed: Minted by this stage as the keeper. T-1533 drew this keeper's own children here — 2 of them — out of the book's `under_10` lodging cells, at the size the 1840 histogram gives the household. What is still owed is a SPOUSE, which no rule this project has made can draw for a keeper who is a woman; the ledger's `keeper_families` row states it, and the staffing under a keeper is T-1183's.
